reserveReview.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-1 (lead usde-ethena)
reserveReview.rationale: Ethena's collateral positions API reports a single 99.0% Liquid Cash aggregate, but the issuer's same-timestamp strategy breakdown API distributes exactly that aggregate across Liquid Stables (45.67%: USDT, USDC, USDtb, PYUSD), DeFi Lending (34.83%: Aave, Morpho), RWA (12.43%: JAAA, STAC), and Institutional Lending (6.08%: BTC-collateralized), with the remaining 0.99% matching the per-asset delta-hedged crypto rows (BTC 0.55%, ETH 0.42%, BNB and LST dust ~0.02%). The curated composition therefore replaces the prior aggregate Liquid Cash row with the issuer-published strategy categories. Per-constituent weights inside the stablecoin and RWA categories are not published, so those two categories stay bounded as baskets.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Ethena real-time collateral positions API crossed with the same-timestamp issuer strategy breakdown API (snapshot 2026-07-19T15:00:32Z); category weights used as published, no estimates
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The 45.67% Liquid Stables category is an issuer-labeled basket of USDT, USDC, USDtb, and PYUSD without published per-stablecoin weights, and the 12.43% RWA category is a basket of JAAA and STAC fund shares without published per-fund weights. Constituent-level allocation and failure-domain splits for both baskets remain issuer-undisclosed.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: Ethena publishes the category total and constituent list (USDT, USDC, USDtb, PYUSD) but not per-stablecoin weights, so no single tracked coinId can be linked without fabrication.
Aave and Morpho lending market positions are protocol exposures, not tracked stablecoin dependencies.
Ethena discloses the two fund identities (JAAA and STAC) but not their relative weights inside the RWA category, so the slice cannot be linked to one tracked coinId.
BTC-collateralized loans to undisclosed institutional borrowers are external private-credit exposure, not a tracked stablecoin dependency.
BTC, ETH, and BNB backing with paired derivatives hedges are external crypto exposures rather than tracked stablecoin dependencies.

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-1 (lead usde-ethena)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: Ethena names Copper, Ceffu, and Fireblocks as off-exchange settlement providers and states that protocol assets remain beneficially owned by the protocol, while Copper and Ceffu use commingled omnibus wallets. Provider allocation shares across the stablecoin, DeFi lending, RWA, institutional lending, and crypto-basis categories, and contractual outcomes in each provider or exchange insolvency, are not public.
